title: bug: nothing stops an agent session's porcelain `git commit` in the shared control checkout — a subagent's failed `cd` committed 4 peers' WIP as "D" and a landing pushed it
description:
Incident on 2026-10-30 at 13:27:12Z: worker-0062feec (task-30066ccd, WT-S) launched a review subagent. The subagent ran a scratch command in the repo root after its `cd` into a scratch dir failed, and that command made commit f6da2d7f "D" on moe/work-2026-10-24. The commit took every modified or staged tracked file, 71 in all:
- unreviewed in-progress bytes from task-f31d415d (scripts/moe-agent.sh/.ps1, postflight.sh), task-b1aecb54 (proposeRail.ts/.test.ts, docs), task-71516084 (local-runner) and WT-S;
- 2 human-staged root files;
- 57 .moe/ paths.

Two minutes later the next wrapper landing (91eaa6ae) pushed it to origin. Every idle sh seat then hot-reloaded the unreviewed wrapper bytes, because 5998f871 now trusts "committed" bytes. Each affected task's own landing found its paths already clean, so per-task attribution and QA's commit evidence broke.

The rule "wrappers are the only Git writers" is prompt-only. Nothing in the checkout enforces it.

Expected: a porcelain `git commit` (and, ideally, `git push`) run from inside an agent session in the control checkout is refused, with a message saying the wrapper lands the work.
- The wrapper's own landings must still work. A human committing outside any agent session must still work.
- One possible shape: a hook installed via core.hooksPath pointing at a tracked hooks dir, which refuses when MOE_WORKER_ID (or a dedicated marker the wrappers export to CLIs) is set and the wrapper's landing marker is not. The architect decides the shape.
- Account for both launchers (sh and ps1 twins) and for the settings.commitHooks semantics.
definitionOfDone: Inside a launched agent session (sh and ps1 seats), a porcelain `git commit` in the control checkout is refused with a message naming the wrapper landing rule. A regression test reproduces the 2026-10-30 shape: a scratch command run in the control checkout after a failed cd.
Wrapper completion and checkpoint landings, and a human's commit made outside any agent session, still succeed. Postflight harnesses (sh and ps1) and the parity check pass.
docs (scripts/CLAUDE.md Land on every exit, plus TROUBLESHOOTING) describe the guard and how a human bypasses it deliberately.

implementationPlan.description: Read mem:task-task-c4cd6dce82bf49648dafdd9c538ff328-handoff and use test-driven-development. Add a compact parameterized node:test harness driving the REAL sh/ps1 wrappers with the existing postflight-fake-proxy.js and fake CLI, not just extracted guard functions. Every fixture is an absolute temp path; all setup git commands use explicit cwd/-C and check exit status. The fake CLI deliberately runs a nested shell with a failed scratch cd followed by ordinary git commit -am D (without errexit), plus staged-only commit, and attempts a push to a disposable local bare remote. Assert refusal text names wrapper landing, HEAD/remote refs and staged/dirty peer+human sentinels are unchanged before postflight. Include control subdirectory/git -C access, a separate scratch repo and linked worktree where ordinary hooks still operate, spaces/Unicode/path metacharacters, and native Windows Git/PowerShell 5.1 cases. Keep one shared fixture and bounded/redacted logs; do not edit the held-out or shared postflight suites.

Implement twin agent Git-guard preparation using native Git process-scoped configuration, never persistent git config or installed-hook replacement. Resolve the control checkout's absolute gitdir and existing effective hook directory BEFORE adding the overlay. In a per-seat secure temp directory generate LF/no-BOM shell hooks and a tiny config setting core.hooksPath. Append an includeIf.gitdir:<exact escaped absolute control gitdir>.path entry through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n; use Git-compatible Windows paths/case handling, no trailing-slash recursive match, and escape Git wildmatch/config/shell syntax independently. Existing caller config entries remain intact. Generate pre-commit/pre-push refusal hooks with MOE_AGENT_GIT_REFUSED and 'the wrapper lands the work'; only explicit MOE_ALLOW_AGENT_GIT_WRITES=1 delegates to the original hook. Forward other installed executable hooks to their original absolute files with unchanged args/stdin/status, not copied bodies or eval. Preserve original hook failures on bypass. Validate the effective hooksPath using the actual prospective child env. Error handling: failed identity/config/temp/permission/validation means MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and no CLI launch, never an unprotected fallback. Non-Git projects remain supported without claiming Git protection.

Apply the prepared environment at every real CLI invocation (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Grok/custom command, interactive/headless, taskless notification and loop/reload paths), preserving command args, stdin/TTY, pipeline exit status and account environment. Use child subshell scope on sh; PS saves/restores only its own appended runtime-config entries in a finally before wrapper postflight/teardown, including launch failure/cancellation. Do not globally export the guard into wrapper Git or sidecars. Extend the new tests to prove normal completion with commitHooks=false and true, checkpoint plumbing, original hook denial, explicit one-command human bypass, ordinary human commit outside the session, concurrent seats with separate guard temps, and caller GIT_CONFIG_COUNT restoration (including existing core.hooksPath). Verify spawned descendant shells inherit the guard; document explicit env/config stripping as deliberate bypass, not a sandbox guarantee. Reuse existing secure-temp lifecycle; no .moe writes, no PATH git shim, no general Git protocol changes. Keep guard files alive through the CLI and remove only the seat's own temp files after exit.

Document the accidental-write guard under scripts/CLAUDE.md 'Land on every exit' and a focused TROUBLESHOOTING entry. Explain control-only scope, wrapper-only landing, setup-failure diagnostic, settings.commitHooks unchanged, original human hooks unchanged, and that this is not a malicious-agent sandbox (--no-verify/explicit hooksPath or removing inherited Git config can bypass). Show a deliberately scoped human override in bash and PowerShell with restoration in finally; do not teach agents to use the bypass as their normal repair. Use cd ... && git ... or git -C absolute-path for all scratch examples.

Run the concentrated verification gate fresh: node --test scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && npm run docs:lint . Submit its exact command/exitCode/outputTail as completion evidence. Also require native Windows execution of the new node test and node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell (no PS skip counted as a pass); inspect supported-launch argv/environment across all four CLI paths. New tests must fail with the guard removed and demonstrate the incident failure before the fix; current harnesses pass unchanged. Report platform availability honestly rather than substituting Linux pwsh for Windows Git/PS5.1.

Final adversarial self-review of this task's diff: can a failed cd/nested shell hit the control checkout, can an inherited config override silently disable hooks, can glob/case/path quoting affect another repo, can two seats remove each other's guards, and can cancellation leak the guard into wrapper hook commits? Confirm no persistent Git config/hook edits, no peer index changes, no credentials/config values in logs, and exact restoration on success/failure. Check task-owned net growth <=400 lines, no borrowed lane edits, and preserve Bash grouped-loop/reload fences. Correct any finding and rerun the named gate before complete_task; hand off to QA, never approve your own work.

reopenReason: Governor promote under the human's 13:00Z delegation. This is the guard for the f6da2d7f "D" incident. The risk of a repeat is high while the WT epic runs many scratch-git tests. If the plan touches scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}, it joins the serialized wrapper lane; ask a governor for the edge.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen native process-scoped Git conditional include and temporary forwarding hooks. Persistent core.hooksPath install would race seats and alter human hooks; MOE_WORKER_ID alone also reaches wrapper hook-enabled commits; PATH git shims miss absolute Git and are unnecessary. Optional push guard shares the same small mechanism. No API/schema change.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Wrappers export MOE_WORKER_ID globally, so it is insufficient to distinguish CLI from wrapper. sh apply_account_env is already child scoped but Codex/Gemini/Grok call sites differ; PS dispatch uses several try/finally paths. Existing postflight-fake-proxy.js can supply all fixture behavior without edits. Linux scratch probe with exact includeIf gitdir refused control commit, allowed scratch+human commits and left local config unchanged. Official Git githooks/git-config document config precedence, gitdir matching and bypass limits. Official Codex config reference documents shell_environment_policy filters: do not claim this guard survives deliberate custom removal of inherited runtime Git config.
planningNotes.risks: Accidental peer-WIP publication/data loss justifies max effort. Governor msg-c25d45... assigns wrapper lane after task-01f37ac63316409ab581f5a189002cb8 and before task-724e31fadd3e4f5cb137abe9e4147f11; governor will wire edges from submitted files. WT-04T remains parallel because fixture untouched. Five files, six steps; keep implementation small via native Git config and shared parameterized tests, <=60 human-equivalent min/400 net lines. CLI/shell explicit config/environment stripping and no-verify remain deliberate bypasses; not an isolation security boundary. Windows CRLF, shell hook quoting, wildcard escaping and PS cleanup are required coverage.
